issue.title: Admin editor rejects an entire paste when a Google Docs table has an aligned cell or a merged cell (TableCellSafety)
issue.body:
### Description Since the table paste safety check landed (#2934, `packages/admin/src/components/editor/TableCellSafety.ts`), pasting rich text that contains a table from Google Docs into a Portable Text field in the admin editor is rejected **as a whole** whenever the table has either: 1. a cell whose paragraph carries `text-align` (any centred or right-aligned cell), or 2. a merged cell (`colspan`) together with a `` (Google Docs always emits one). Nothing is inserted, not even the paragraphs around the table, and the editor shows: "This table has unsupported cell formatting, merged cells, or column widths. Paste it as plain text or simplify the table and try again." Expected: the paste lands and the editor keeps what it can represent, dropping the alignment or the merge (which is what 0.34 did), or at least inserts the non-table content and reports only the table. Rejecting the entire paste pushes editors to "paste as plain text", which loses every heading, link and mark in the draft. Verified on `emdash` / `@emdash-cms/admin` 1.1.0 against 0.34.0 with the same clipboard payloads (dispatched `paste` ClipboardEvent and real clipboard + Ctrl+V in headless Chromium gave identical results). The same code is present in 1.2.0 and on `main`. Why, from reading the bundle and the source: - `cellContentStatus` returns `invalid-table` as soon as a cell paragraph has `attrs.textAlign` set. The TextAlign extension sets it from `style="text-align:…"` on paste, so any aligned cell fails. - `validColumnWidths(colwidth, colspan)` requires `colwidth.length === colspan`. TipTap's `parseColgroupWidth` (in `@tiptap/extension-table`) yields a single `[width]` for a cell even when it spans two columns, so a Docs merge with a `` always fails. Word emits no ``, so a Word merge alone passes while a Word centred cell still fails. Pastes without a table, and tables without alignment or merges (column widths included), behave identically on 0.34 and 1.1. ### Steps to reproduce 1. On a site running emdash 1.1.0 (or 1.2.0), open an entry with a Portable Text field in the admin editor and place the cursor in an empty top-level paragraph. 2. Paste HTML with `text/html` set to the Google Docs style payload below (a heading, a paragraph with bold, and a 2x2 table with a centred header row): ```html

Heading

Intro with bold text.

Header A

Header B

Row1 A

Row1 B

 ``` 3. Observe: nothing is inserted, the heading and paragraph included, and the message above appears. 4. Remove the two `text-align:center;` styles and paste again: everything lands, table included. 5. Variant for merged cells: keep the `` and make the first header cell `` with no alignment anywhere: rejected again. Remove the `` (Word-style payload): accepted. 6. On 0.34.0 the payloads from steps 2 and 5 are both accepted; the alignment or the merge is dropped silently. ### Environment - emdash version: 1.1.0 (`@emdash-cms/admin` 1.1.0; same code in 1.2.0 and `main`); regression from 0.34.0 - Node.js version: 24 (Astro node adapter, standalone server) - Runtime: Node - OS: Linux (reproduction in headless Chromium via Playwright) ### Screenshots Not applicable. The visible result is the rejection message quoted above with an unchanged document; I can attach the editor screenshots from the reproduction on request. ### Logs / error output ```shell Editor message after paste: This table has unsupported cell formatting, merged cells, or column widths. Paste it as plain text or simplify the table and try again. ```
